original_question: For the same orthogonally invariant class C~^2(D_d), it is known that the integration problem suffers from the curse of dimensionality for certain domains D_d having small radius, including l_p^d balls with p>=2. Does the curse of dimensionality also hold when D_d is an l_p^d ball with p<2?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Example 1 (following Remark 8): the open subcase of the conjectured uniform lower bound (14) for the orthogonally invariant class \widetilde{C}^2(D_d), namely the unresolved question in comment 2 whether the curse of dimensionality holds when D_d is a volume-normalized \ell_p^d-ball with p<2.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant function class as the orthogonally invariant class \widetilde{C}^2(D_d), the known positive result for certain small-radius domains including volume-normalized \ell_p^d-balls with p\ge 2, and the unresolved p<2 case. It also correctly focuses on the curse-of-dimensionality question rather than a broader tractability issue.
missing_details: The paper works with worst-case numerical integration over open sets D_d\subset \mathbb{R}^d of Lebesgue measure 1; this normalization should be stated explicitly.

The class must be defined explicitly: \widetilde{C}^2(D_d)=\{f\in C^2(D_d): \|f\|_\infty\le 1, \operatorname{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2}, \operatorname{Lip}(D^\theta f)\le d^{-1}\ \text{for every }\theta\in S^{d-1}\}.
The directional derivative notation D^\theta f should be defined, with \theta ranging over the Euclidean unit sphere S^{d-1}.
The Lipschitz constant \operatorname{Lip}(g) is taken with respect to the Euclidean norm on D_d; this is part of the paper's orthogonally invariant setup.
The domains in the open question are not arbitrary \ell_p^d-balls, but volume-normalized open \ell_p^d-balls in \mathbb{R}^d.
The paper's nearest official formulation is stronger than merely asking for the curse: it conjectures a uniform lower bound e(n,\widetilde{C}^2(D_d))\ge C n^{-2/d} with C independent of d and D_d.
The quantifiers should be stated: the conjectural lower bound is for all n,d\in \mathbb{N}, with a constant C>0 independent of n, d, and the admissible domains D_d.
The draft does not specify whether p is fixed in [1,2) or whether the claim is meant uniformly for all such p; the paper's comment is about the regime p<2 for these balls.

The meaning of 'the curse of dimensionality' should be made stand-alone, e.g. exponential growth of the information complexity n(\varepsilon,\widetilde{C}^2(D_d)) in d for some fixed error threshold \varepsilon\in(0,1).
The paper's context is real-valued functions on real domains, not abstract orthogonally invariant objects; that ambient setting should be stated.
refined_question:
Let D_d\subset \mathbb{R}^d be the open volume-normalized \ell_p^d-ball (so \lambda_d(D_d)=1) for some p\in[1,2). For the worst-case numerical integration problem over the orthogonally invariant class
\widetilde{C}^2(D_d)=\{f\in C^2(D_d): \|f\|_\infty\le 1,\ \operatorname{Lip}(f)\le d^{-1/2},\ \operatorname{Lip}(D^\theta f)\le d^{-1}\ \text{for every }\theta\in S^{d-1}\},
where \operatorname{Lip}(g)=\sup_{x,y\in D_d,\,x\ne y}|g(x)-g(y)|/\|x-y\|_2 and D^\theta f is the directional derivative in direction \theta, does there exist a constant C>0, independent of n, d, and D_d, such that
 e(n,\widetilde{C}^2(D_d))\ge C\,n^{-2/d}\quad\text{for all }n,d\in\mathbb{N}?
In particular, does numerical integration over \widetilde{C}^2(D_d) suffer from the curse of dimensionality for volume-normalized \ell_p^d-balls with p<2?
justification: The draft is clearly targeting Section 4 rather than any introductory conjecture: Remark 8 introduces the orthogonally invariant normed class, and Example 1 gives the exact class \widetilde{C}^2(D_d), the conjectured uniform lower bound (14), and then explicitly singles out in comment 2 the unresolved case of \ell_p^d-balls with p<2. Since the paper's nearest official formulation is the stronger lower-bound conjecture e(n,\widetilde{C}^2(D_d))\ge C n^{-2/d}, the refined question specializes that conjecture to the p<2 ball regime while preserving the paper's original intent. The user's draft asks only for the curse, which is a weaker consequence of the paper's stated conjectural lower bound.
